summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen's famous silk hat, which had been in the possession of Lieut. Col. Lord Barrington, was returned to Allen's heirs after Barrington's arrest. The hat was authenticated by Paddy Nalty, who had worked for Allen for six years.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, July 19, 1903, page 2.

facts.fact: After Allen's death, 'Lieut. Col. Lord Barrington' wore Allen's silk hat and refused to give it up to Tillie Hartgrove, Allen's housekeeper, who claimed it as a keepsake
Hartgrove and J. W. Gillespie went to Clayton and failed to get Barrington to surrender the hat; Barrington denied having it, and they left threatening a replevin suit
Barrington returned Allen's hat by messenger boy with a note reading 'From Barington'; Paddy Nalty, who worked for Allen six years, pronounced it genuine
The hat was put on display for Allen's friends along with the silver cup he won with the English heavyweight championship in 1878

notes: Printed headline matches the database text. Barrington was jailed on a charge of murdering James P. McCann. The article calls Hartgrove the housekeeper and Gillespie is the man who originally outfitted Barrington. Facts index 089 covers the hat dispute earlier.
